newsitem.title: FRANCE: Monaco names Algiers ambassador as prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Monaco names Algiers ambassador as prime minister.

text.p: Prince Rainier of Monaco has named France's ambassador to Algiers, Michel Leveque, to succeed Prime Minister Paul Dijoud, the principality said on Thursday.
It said in a brief statement that Leveque would take office on February 3.

The French Foreign Ministry said earlier this month that Dijoud, officially titled Minister of State and the head of a five-strong cabinet, would take up a new post preparing a visit by President Jacques Chirac to Latin America in March.
Rainier, who rules over a population of just 30,000 and less than two square km (one square mile) of territory nestled on the French Riviera, chooses cabinet members from a list proposed by Paris.
At a news conference earlier this month, Dijoud urged greater cooperation with France, the United States and Italy in cracking down on money laundering.

Described by British writer Somerset Maugham as "the sunny place for shady people", tax-free Monaco is feared to be vulnerable to money laundering given its banking secrecy rules, its proximity to Italian organised crime and its casinos.

The announcement of Dijoud's departure came just two weeks after Monaco launched a 10-month birthday party to fete the 700th anniversary of the state, known more for its glamorous royal family than its politics.
